name: Sonamukhi
kitchenUse: Not a kitchen herb; taken as tablets or a tea at bedtime for occasional constipation.

typicalUse.adultAmount: Follow the label; use for no more than a week without a doctor
typicalUse.note: Gentler options such as isabgol, fluids and fibre come first.

cautions.note: Never use with stomach pain of unknown cause, blocked bowel, appendicitis or inflammatory bowel disease. Long use causes dependence and loss of potassium.
Do not give to children without a doctor's advice.
Use in pregnancy or while breastfeeding only if your doctor advises.
High doses taken for a long time have caused liver injury.
Potassium loss from overuse can upset the heart rhythm.

interactions.effect: Together they can lower potassium too far.

evidence.summary: An established laxative for short-term constipation, available as a standard over-the-counter medicine.
